name: Vowel
author: Emilie Gillet
description: Braids' table-driven vowel synthesizer: three formants read at sixteen steps a cycle, gated by a ramp that restarts every pitch period, through a tanh shaper. The stepped ancestor of Speech's SAM mode.

controls.label: Spread
controls.description: Pulls the upper two formants toward the first or pushes them apart, past the vowels in the module's list.

controls.label: Shift
controls.description: Scales all three formants together, from a large vocal tract to a small one.

controls.label: Vowel
controls.description: Walks the nine phoneme frames, crossfading between neighbours.

controls.label: Grain
controls.description: Shortens or stretches the burst inside each pitch period, from a tight grain to a ramp still open at the reset.

outputs.main: Mono: the shaped formant stack. Stereo: the shaped stack with a small downward formant shift on the left.
outputs.aux: Mono: the clean stack ahead of the overdrive. Stereo: the shaped stack with a small upward formant shift on the right.

trigger: Selects and articulates a new consonant without resetting the oscillator or formant phases.
